evidence: supabase/catalog/products/*.json: 210 of 1,250 items have no brand (e.g. 'HMT Rice 1 kg', 'Horse Gram 500 g', 'Makki Atta 500 g' in atta-rice-dal.json). supabase/catalog/family-classification.csv lists an 'Unbranded Option' for many families. Nothing in the schema or admin covers packing batches or labels.

title: Push notifications: silent failure in store builds, no tap action, sent to the wrong person after logout
detail: getExpoPushTokenAsync() is called with no projectId and there are no FCM credentials, so store builds get no token. The error is swallowed by console.warn. Tapping a notification does not open the order, even though the payload carries order_id. Messages are sent without channelId, so the high-priority 'orders' channel is never used. Logout does not delete the push_tokens row (primary key is user_id + token), so the previous user's order alerts keep arriving on a shared phone.
needs_from_owner: Firebase project for FCM (Android) and an Apple push key (iOS)
evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts:35 (no projectId) and the console.warn catch. app.json has no googleServicesFile or expo-notifications plugin. Searched the app for addNotificationResponseReceivedListener / useLastNotificationResponse: none. supabase/functions/notify-order/index.ts:49 payload has no channelId. apps/mobile/src/stores/auth.ts signOut does not touch push_tokens. supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql:352-358.
verifier_note: Confirmed. apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts:35 calls getExpoPushTokenAsync() with no projectId; it would read extra.eas.projectId, which is missing (item 9), and the catch only does console.warn. app.json has no googleServicesFile or expo-notifications plugin entry, and FCM V1 and APNs credentials still have to be uploaded to EAS. No addNotificationResponseReceivedListener or useLastNotificationResponse anywhere. notify-order/index.ts sends {to,title,body,sound,data} with no channelId, so the 'orders' channel is never used. signOut in stores/auth.ts leaves push_tokens alone, and the PK is (user_id, token) at 0001:352-358, so the old user's row stays and their order alerts reach the next user on a shared phone. Order status still updates live through realtime on order/[id].tsx, which is why this is important rather than blocking.

title: No recovery when an online payment fails
detail: Orders left in 'pending_payment' get no 'retry payment' button, and the order page says 'Paid via online payment' even when nothing was paid. They also hold reserved stock forever, because no job expires them. If verify-payment fails after the money was taken, the app creates a new idempotency key, so tapping again can create a second order and a second charge. This becomes a launch-blocker the day online payments are switched on.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/cart.tsx onError (regenerates idempotencyKey unless the error says cancelled). apps/mobile/src/app/order/[id].tsx 'Paid via' line ignores status. supabase/migrations/0003_orders_rpc.sql:131 reserves stock; searched for pg_cron / expire: none.
verifier_note: Mostly confirmed, with partial mitigations. No retry-payment button exists, and order/[id].tsx 'Paid via online payment' ignores status. No pg_cron or expiry job exists, so pending_payment orders keep their reserved stock. In the cart.tsx onError path a fresh idempotency key is created unless the message says 'cancelled', which allows a second order and a second charge. Mitigations the reviewer missed: razorpay-webhook confirms payment.captured server-side, so a paid order still moves to placed if verify-payment fails, and customers can cancel pending_payment orders themselves (packages/api/src/status.ts:39) to release stock. payment.failed only marks the payment row and leaves the order and stock alone. Becomes a launch-blocker when Razorpay is turned on. The orphan-order problem that exists today is covered under item 7.

title: A closed store looks like 'we don't deliver here'
detail: find_serving_store skips stores with is_open = false, so a store that is closed for the night or paused shows the 'We are not here yet / Not serviceable' screen instead of 'Closed now, opens at 6:00'. opens_at and closes_at are returned to the app but never used, and place_order does not enforce them either.
needs_from_owner: Store operating hours
evidence: supabase/migrations/0002_lat_lng_columns.sql:71 'where s.is_open'. packages/api/src/stores.ts returns opens_at and closes_at. Searching apps/mobile/src for opens_at / closes_at / is_open: nothing. apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx unserviceable notice.
verifier_note: Confirmed. find_serving_store (0002_lat_lng_columns.sql:71) filters on s.is_open, so serving_store returns nothing and the app shows the '(tabs)/index.tsx' 'We are not here yet' notice. opens_at and closes_at are returned by packages/api/src/stores.ts but are used only in apps/admin/src/app/stores. place_order (0003) enforces is_open (STORE_CLOSED) but not the opening hours. Cheap fix: return closed stores with a flag, show 'Closed, opens at 6:00', and enforce hours in place_order.

title: Missing error, retry and offline handling
detail: No screen checks query errors. If the delivery-area check fails on a first launch, Home spins forever. A failed orders request shows 'No orders yet', and a failed product request shows 'not available at your store'. Address search uses try/finally with no catch, so errors are never handled. There is no error boundary (a crash leaves a blank screen) and no offline banner.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx (spinner while !storeId; the status 'error' state is never shown). apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/orders.tsx ListEmptyComponent. apps/mobile/src/app/location/index.tsx autocomplete effect and onSuggestion. Searching the app for isError / ErrorBoundary / NetInfo finds only RateItem.
verifier_note: Confirmed. In (tabs)/index.tsx the spinner shows while !storeId and the status 'error' set by stores/location.ts refreshStore is never rendered, so a first launch spins forever. Returning users keep their persisted store. In (tabs)/orders.tsx a failed query falls into ListEmptyComponent 'No orders yet'. In product/[slug].tsx an error shows 'not available at your store'. location/index.tsx uses try/finally with no catch in both the autocomplete effect and onSuggestion. isError appears only in RateItem. There is no ErrorBoundary export and no NetInfo or offline banner. lib/query.ts sets retry: 1.

title: No crash reporting
detail: Crashes and JS errors in store builds are invisible. The only logging is console.warn in push.ts.
needs_from_owner: Crash-reporting account (e.g. Sentry free tier)
evidence: Searched apps/mobile (src, package.json, app.json) for sentry / crashlytics / bugsnag: none.
verifier_note: Confirmed. No sentry, crashlytics or bugsnag in apps/mobile package.json, app.json or src. The only logging is console.warn in lib/push.ts. Cheap to add with @sentry/react-native and its Expo plugin, and it should go into the first store build.

title: Cart shows stale prices and stock
detail: Cart lines keep the price and stock from the moment they were added, saved on the device with no expiry, and are never refreshed. place_order re-prices on the server, so a cash-on-delivery customer can be charged a different total than the one shown, with no 'prices changed' warning. Reorder copies old prices with available: 50 and an empty slug. Changing to an address served by a different store keeps the old store's lines.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/stores/cart.ts (CartLine.price and available are set once in add()). apps/mobile/src/app/order/[id].tsx reorder(). supabase/migrations/0003_orders_rpc.sql:133 re-prices from inventory.
verifier_note: Confirmed with one nuance. stores/cart.ts sets price and available once in add() and keeps them in AsyncStorage forever. cart.tsx computes the bill from those values and never refetches. place_order re-prices from inventory (0003:133) and the customer sees the new total only on the order page. reorder() in order/[id].tsx uses slug '' and available: 50. Nuance: add() wipes the cart when storeId changes, so old-store lines go on the next add, but checkout never compares cart.storeId with the current store. Fix: re-quote lines on cart open and warn when prices change.

title: No rider contact or delivery handover check
detail: The order page shows no rider name, phone or call button, and there is no delivery OTP or PIN to confirm handover. Both are standard on Blinkit and Zepto and help with cash orders. order_events is fetched but the timeline with timestamps is never shown.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/order/[id].tsx (only rider_id is passed to the map). packages/api/src/orders.ts get() selects order_events but the screen never renders them. Searched migrations for a delivery otp / pin / handover: none.
verifier_note: Confirmed. order/[id].tsx passes only rider_id to MapOrFallback and shows no name, phone or call button. RLS 'profiles self read' (0001:420) would also block customers from reading the rider profile, so an RPC or masked-number approach is needed. No delivery OTP or PIN in migrations or the rider app. ordersApi.get selects order_events, but neither the mobile app nor the website renders them.

title: Address search will not work in production without Ola Maps
detail: Without an Ola key the provider is 'device', and its autocomplete always returns [], so the address search box does nothing. The Ola response mapping is marked unverified in the code. The public Nominatim, Photon and OSM tile servers are for testing only.
needs_from_owner: Ola Maps API key, restricted to the app
evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/maps.ts (header comment 'verify field names against the live docs'; autocomplete returns [] for device). apps/mobile/src/lib/env.ts mapsProvider defaults to 'device'.
verifier_note: Confirmed. apps/mobile/src/lib/maps.ts:167 returns [] for autocomplete when the provider is 'device' or there is no Ola key, and the header says to verify the Ola field names against the live docs. env.ts defaults mapsProvider to 'device'. Also, without Ola the live tracking map uses https://tile.openstreetmap.org (packages/api/src/mapStyle.ts:18), whose usage policy does not allow production app traffic. Not a blocker because GPS detect, pin confirm and the manual form still work. An Ola key and a live check fix it.

title: No over-the-air updates or forced upgrade
detail: eas.json names update channels, but expo-updates is not installed and there is no runtimeVersion. Every fix (including legal text) therefore needs a store release, and old versions cannot be forced to upgrade. The version label is hard-coded as 'RATION v0.1.0'.
evidence: apps/mobile/package.json (no expo-updates). apps/mobile/app.json (no updates or runtimeVersion). apps/mobile/eas.json channel entries. apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx version caption.
verifier_note: Confirmed. expo-updates is not in apps/mobile/package.json, app.json has no updates or runtimeVersion, but eas.json defines development, preview and production channels. account.tsx hard-codes 'RATION v0.1.0' instead of reading expo-constants. There is no minimum-version check. Important because installs from a build without expo-updates can never receive OTA, so it has to be in the first store build.

title: Login required before browsing
detail: All tabs are blocked until login, so new users must give their phone number before seeing a single product. Blinkit and Zepto let you browse first and log in at checkout. Apple guideline 5.1.1 can also reject apps that force sign-up for features that do not need an account.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx: Stack.Protected guard={status === "signed_in"} wraps (tabs).
verifier_note: Confirmed. apps/mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx wraps (tabs) in Stack.Protected guard={status==='signed_in'}. The backend already supports anonymous browsing: catalog, stores and inventory policies allow anon reads (0001 'public catalog: anyone (including anon)'), so this is an app-only change that asks for login at checkout. Real Apple 5.1.1 rejection risk for iOS.

title: Referral share text promises the wrong reward
detail: The share message says 'Use my code ... for ₹50 off your first order'. The real reward is ₹50 wallet credit to both people after the first order is delivered, so the promise is misleading. The code can only be entered on the profile screen after sign-up, there is no install-referral link, and there are no abuse checks.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx share(). supabase/migrations/0004_referrals_reviews_search.sql:4,31-41 (5000 paise credit on delivery). apps/mobile/src/app/account/profile.tsx is the only place to enter the code.
verifier_note: Confirmed. The account.tsx share() message says '₹50 off your first order', and the referral row caption says 'they get ₹50 off'. 0004_referrals_reviews_search.sql:31-41 actually credits 5000 paise to both wallets after the first delivered order, which matches the profile.tsx text. The code can be entered only on profile.tsx. There is no install referral and no abuse limits beyond blocking self-referral in apply_referral_code, and item 1 bypasses even that. The text fix is trivial and should be done before launch. The rest can wait.

title: Rider app breaks Play's background-location rules
detail: The partner app asks for background location straight after the foreground prompt, with no in-app explanation screen first. Google Play requires that disclosure, plus a background-location declaration and a demo video in the Play Console. The rider app also lacks privacy policy links and account deletion, which Play requires.
needs_from_owner: Play Console background-location declaration and a demo video
evidence: apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts requestLocationPermissions() calls requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync() right after the foreground grant. apps/rider/src/stores/rider.ts:25 only shows 'Allow location access...' after a failure. apps/rider/app.json declares ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION.
verifier_note: Confirmed. apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts requestLocationPermissions() calls requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync() straight after the foreground grant, with no disclosure screen first. apps/rider/src/stores/rider.ts shows 'Allow location access...' only after a failure. apps/rider/app.json declares ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION. There is no legal screen and no account deletion in apps/rider/src. Priority lowered: this blocks launch only if the partner app goes on the public Play listing. A small in-house fleet can install an EAS internal APK first. The disclosure screen itself is only a few hours of work.

title: No error tracking, uptime checks or alerts
detail: There is no Sentry or similar in any app or function. Edge functions only console.error, and Supabase keeps logs briefly. If a Razorpay refund fails after cancel-order has already cancelled the order, no refunds row is written and nobody is alerted. notify-order failures only show up in net._http_response. The web app has no error.tsx or global-error page, and nothing checks the site, the Supabase API or the functions from outside.
needs_from_owner: Sentry account (free tier is enough to start) and an uptime service account
evidence: Searching for sentry|bugsnag|datadog|logtail|posthog|crashlytics|uptime|healthcheck finds nothing. supabase/functions/_shared/http.ts errorResponse only logs. In supabase/functions/cancel-order/index.ts, createRazorpayRefund runs after the cancel_order RPC with no compensation. No error.tsx or not-found.tsx under apps/web/src/app.
verifier_note: Confirmed. There is no sentry, bugsnag, posthog or crashlytics in any package.json or the lockfile. supabase/functions/_shared/http.ts errorResponse only calls console.error. In cancel-order/index.ts, createRazorpayRefund runs after the cancel_order RPC with no compensation. There is no error.tsx, global-error.tsx or not-found.tsx in web or admin, and no +not-found in the Expo apps. New bug found: staff cancellations never refund online payments. staff_cancel_order (0005_staff_rpcs.sql:21-32) returns refund_online, but the admin calls the RPC directly (packages/api/src/admin.ts:150), drops the result, and no Razorpay refund or refunds row is ever created. This does not bite under a cash or UPI-on-delivery launch, but must be fixed before online payments are switched on.

title: No staging environment
detail: There is only the local test stack and a future production project. No staging Supabase project, no EAS preview profile wired to staging env vars, and no Cloudflare preview deployments, so migrations and app builds would go straight to production.
needs_from_owner: Second Supabase project (extra cost)
evidence: apps/mobile/eas.json preview profile has no env. No staging references in README.md or the workflows. Only one project_id in supabase/config.toml.
verifier_note: Confirmed. supabase/config.toml has one project_id ('ration', local). apps/mobile/eas.json preview has no env. README.md and the workflows have no staging references.

title: No scheduled maintenance jobs
detail: Nothing runs on a schedule. Online orders abandoned in pending_payment keep their stock reserved forever. idempotency_keys and webhook_events grow without limit. Riders who disappear can stay 'online'. There are no daily summary reports for operations.
evidence: Searching for pg_cron|cron.schedule finds nothing. supabase/migrations/0003_orders_rpc.sql:131 reserves stock at order placement; it is released only on the cancel and payment paths (lines ~304, 346). No expiry function for pending_payment.
verifier_note: Nothing in migrations or workflows runs on a schedule (no pg_cron or cron.schedule). place_order reserves stock at 0003_orders_rpc.sql:131. The razorpay-webhook payment.failed branch (razorpay-webhook/index.ts:55-56) only marks the payments row failed, so the order stays in pending_payment with stock reserved until the customer cancels. idempotency_keys and webhook_events are never pruned. Refinement: the 'vanished riders' point is mostly handled already, because auto_assign_rider (0007_auto_assign.sql) only picks riders whose location was updated in the last 10 minutes; stale is_online only skews dashboards. Under a cash or UPI-on-delivery launch no order enters pending_payment, so the expiry job matters once online payments start.

title: No security headers and no extra protection on the admin panel
detail: Neither Next app sets CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options or Referrer-Policy. The admin panel is protected only by phone OTP and the staff role check: no second factor, IP allow-list or Cloudflare Access. images.remotePatterns allows any host ('**') even though every image is unoptimized, so the pattern can be removed or tightened.
needs_from_owner: Cloudflare Zero Trust / Access setup for the admin hostname
evidence: apps/web/next.config.ts and apps/admin/next.config.ts have no headers() and set remotePatterns hostname '**'. The admin gate is client-side in apps/admin/src/components/shell.tsx (isStaff).
verifier_note: Confirmed. Neither next.config.ts has headers(), and both allow remotePatterns hostname '**'. Clarification: the admin's data is protected on the server by RLS and is_staff() checks (0001_init.sql:432-451, staff RPCs), not just by the client gate in apps/admin/src/components/shell.tsx. The real weaknesses are no 2FA and no IP allow-list or Cloudflare Access. Also, is_staff() (0001:393) gives store_staff the same write rights as admin over every store, product, coupon and banner, and over orders through the 'orders staff update' policy, which allows editing any order column directly.

title: No audit log of staff actions
detail: Role changes, price and stock edits, coupon changes, bulk CSV imports and staff cancellations leave no record of who changed what, which matters for disputes, fraud checks and cash reconciliation.
evidence: No audit, activity-log or changed_by table or trigger in supabase/migrations. order_events covers only order status changes (0001_init.sql:284).
verifier_note: Confirmed. Migrations have no audit, activity_log, changed_by or updated_by. staff_set_stock and staff_set_role (0005_staff_rpcs.sql:57-95) write no history. order_events (0001:284) records only status changes with actor_id, and wallet_transactions records only wallet movements. The 'orders staff update' policy lets staff change order rows directly with no trace, which matters for cash reconciliation.

title: DPDP Act consent and data-rights flows missing
detail: Login relies on passive 'By continuing you agree' text. There is no itemised consent notice, no stored consent record, no withdrawal, and no self-service data export or correction beyond name and email. There is also no breach-response procedure and no retention schedule (address snapshots are kept forever). Most DPDP Rules 2025 obligations phase in during 2027 and should be built before then.
needs_from_owner: Legal advisor input on the consent notice and retention periods
evidence: The only consent-like text is at apps/mobile/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx:62, apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx:62 and apps/web/src/app/login/page.tsx:65. No consent table in supabase/migrations.
verifier_note: Confirmed. Consent is only passive text: apps/mobile/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx:62, apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx:62, apps/web/src/app/login/page.tsx:65. There is no consent table, no data export, no retention or purge job (orders.address_snapshot is kept forever), and no breach procedure. Correction already exists for name and email only (the 'profiles self update' policy). Most DPDP Rules obligations take effect in 2027, so this is important, not a launch-blocker.

title: No onboarding checks or agreement for delivery partners
detail: An admin can turn any customer into a rider from the People page with no record of driving licence, vehicle RC, insurance, ID or bank details, and no signed partner agreement. The rider app tells partners 'Payouts are settled weekly to your registered bank account', but no bank account is ever captured (this links to the known payouts item).
needs_from_owner: Partner agreement, KYC policy, and legal advice on gig-worker obligations under the Code on Social Security
evidence: The profiles table (0001_init.sql:34) has no KYC fields. The People role change is in apps/admin/src/app/people/page.tsx. The payout text is in apps/rider/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx.
verifier_note: Confirmed. profiles (0001_init.sql:33-45) has no licence, RC, insurance, ID or bank fields. apps/admin/src/app/people/page.tsx turns anyone into a rider with a role dropdown. apps/rider/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx says 'Payouts are settled weekly to your registered bank account by the store', but no bank account is ever captured (links to the known payouts item). Also worth raising with the legal advisor: aggregator duties for gig workers under the Code on Social Security and Karnataka's 2025 platform gig-workers law, since stores are in Bengaluru.

title: No deployment runbook, go-live checklist or incident playbooks
detail: Docs cover only the local stack. There is no step-by-step production deployment guide and no go-live checklist. There are no playbooks for OTP, payment or map provider outages, a store going offline or a rider shortage, and no handbook for store staff using the admin panel. Some docs have drifted: FEATURE_PARITY says 1,248 sample products while the seed has 1,253.
evidence: docs/ contains only FEATURE_PARITY.md. README.md's 'Getting started' is local-only. docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md says '1,248 sample products'; supabase/seeds/catalog.sql line 2 says '1253 products'.
verifier_note: Confirmed. docs/ contains only FEATURE_PARITY.md, and README 'Getting started' covers only the local stack. Doc drift is wider than reported: FEATURE_PARITY.md:30 says 1,248 products, supabase/catalog/README.md:9 says 1,245, and supabase/seeds/catalog.sql:2 says 1253. README.md's stack table still presents 'Cloudflare Pages' and 'RazorpayX for payouts' as production, though neither exists. There is no admin handbook for store staff.

title: No proof of delivery (OTP, photo or delivered-at location)
detail: A rider can tap 'Delivered' from anywhere. There is no delivery OTP for the customer, no photo, and no check that the rider is near the address. rider_locations keeps only one current row per rider and order_events stores no coordinates, so there is no evidence when a customer says a cash or prepaid order never arrived. The Android 'mocked' (fake GPS) flag on locations is never checked either.
needs_from_owner: Decide policy: OTP on every order or only cash / high-value orders, and the allowed distance from the address
evidence: supabase/migrations/0006_rider.sql rider_advance_order checks only status transitions; rider_locations primary key rider_id (0001_init.sql); order_events has no lat/lng; grep for otp/proof/photo/mocked in apps/rider and supabase finds nothing delivery-related
verifier_note: rider_advance_order (0006) checks only the status step. rider_locations has rider_id as its primary key, one row per rider (0001), and rider_update_location in 0005 overwrites it. order_events has no lat/lng. Nothing in apps/rider or supabase reads the 'mocked' flag, and there is no OTP or photo for delivery. I lowered the priority from launch-blocker: launch is mostly cash on delivery, and once gap 3's ledger exists, a cash order marked delivered without delivery shows up as cash the rider owes. A cheap first step is to save the rider's lat/lng and distance to the address on the 'delivered' event. A delivery OTP can follow for prepaid or high-value orders.

title: Riders can see too much customer personal data
detail: The RLS policy 'orders rider pool read' lets every rider read the address_snapshot (name, phone, full address) and totals of every ready, unassigned order in every store, before accepting it. 'orders read' also gives riders permanent access to past customers' phone numbers and addresses through History. Under the DPDP Act 2023, the pool should show only an area-level summary, and phone and address should be hidden once the delivery is finished.
evidence: supabase/migrations/0006_rider.sql policies 'orders rider pool read' / 'order_items rider pool read'; 0001_init.sql policy 'orders read' (rider_id = auth.uid()); packages/api/src/rider.ts pool()/history() select ORDER_COLUMNS incl. address_snapshot; apps/rider/src/components/OrderTile.tsx shows address in pool
verifier_note: The 0006 policy 'orders rider pool read' (role rider, rider_id null, status ready) has no store or online check. packages/api/src/rider.ts pool() selects ORDER_COLUMNS, which includes address_snapshot, user_id, customer_note and totals. OrderTile.tsx shows line1, line2 and landmark in the pool. The 0001 'orders read' policy (rider_id = auth.uid()) gives permanent access, and history() returns the full address_snapshot, including the phone number. Extra bug I found: myActive() and history() do not filter by rider_id = me. Riders are also customers, and RLS lets them read their own customer orders, so a rider's own grocery orders show up under 'Your deliveries' and History. I set it to important rather than launch-blocker: there is one store with a few known riders at launch, and I believe most DPDP Rules 2025 duties start about 18 months after the November 2025 notification. Fix it before scaling (a pool RPC or view with only area-level data, and phone and address hidden after delivery).

title: No rider onboarding or KYC
detail: A rider must first sign up as a customer somewhere else (the rider app blocks new sign-ups), and then an admin changes their role on the People page. Nothing stores driving licence, vehicle RC or insurance, Aadhaar or PAN, bank or UPI details for payouts, emergency contact, police verification, home store, or acceptance of a partner agreement. Admins also cannot invite a rider by phone number.
needs_from_owner: List of required documents, partner agreement text, and which state gig-worker registration and welfare-fee rules apply
evidence: apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx signInWithOtp shouldCreateUser:false; apps/admin/src/app/people/page.tsx role dropdown only; profiles has no rider fields; grep kyc|licence|vehicle|ifsc|bank_account across supabase/apps finds nothing
verifier_note: apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx signs in with shouldCreateUser:false. not-partner.tsx tells the person to ask the store manager. apps/admin/src/app/people/page.tsx only has a role dropdown on existing profiles (staff_set_role in 0005). README 'Staff access' confirms that riders are customers given the rider role. A grep for kyc, licence, vehicle, ifsc, bank_account, aadhaar or emergency in supabase, apps and packages finds nothing rider-related. Paper KYC can work for the first few riders, so this is not a blocker.

title: No earnings model or payout records
detail: rider_summary returns only delivery counts, today's tips and today's cash. There is no pay per delivery or per km, no incentives, no weekly statement and no payout history. Tips on prepaid orders that are owed to riders are not tracked as payable. The Account tab says 'Payouts are settled weekly to your registered bank account', but no bank account is stored anywhere. The login screen promises 'earn per drop', but nothing calculates it. This refines the known 'rider payouts' item.
needs_from_owner: Pay structure (per drop, distance, incentives), payout method (manual bank/UPI or RazorpayX/Cashfree payouts), TDS handling
evidence: supabase/migrations/0006_rider.sql rider_summary; apps/rider/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx payout caption; apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx tagline; docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md 'Rider and vendor payouts ... not implemented'
verifier_note: rider_summary (0006) returns only delivered_today, tips_today, cod_collected_today, delivered_total and is_online. apps/rider/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx says 'Payouts are settled weekly to your registered bank account by the store', but no bank details are stored. The (auth)/index.tsx tagline promises 'earn per drop and tips'. docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md lists payouts as not implemented. Settling by hand works at launch, but the two misleading lines of copy should be changed now, which takes minutes.

title: No failed-delivery or 'report a problem' flow after pickup
detail: After pickup the only button is 'Delivered' (decline is allowed only before pickup). There is no 'customer not reachable', wrong address, refused or damaged option, and no return-to-store status. The order stays out_for_delivery. Because rider_busy_statuses includes that status, the rider gets no automatic orders until staff cancel the order in admin.
needs_from_owner: Policy for how long to wait at the door, cash refusals and returned goods
evidence: packages/api/src/rider.ts RIDER_CAN_DECLINE = accepted/packing/ready, RIDER_NEXT; apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx actions; order_status enum has no failed/returned; 0007_auto_assign.sql rider_busy_statuses
verifier_note: packages/api/src/rider.ts RIDER_CAN_DECLINE is accepted, packing and ready. RIDER_NEXT has no failure step. The order_status enum in 0001 has no failed or returned status. rider_busy_statuses (0007) includes out_for_delivery. Correction: staff do not have to cancel. staff_assign_rider (0005) accepts a null rider at any status, so the admin order screens can also unassign or reassign the rider, and staff_cancel_order works on an out_for_delivery order. Cancelling releases the reserved stock, so goods return to the store. Still, the rider app gives no way to report the problem, and there is no return-to-store record.

title: Riders waiting with the phone locked drop out of automatic assignment
detail: The 60-second heartbeat is a JS setInterval that only runs while the app is open, as the code comment admits. The background task uses distanceInterval 25, so a rider standing still at the dark store sends no updates. auto_assign_rider only considers riders heard from in the last 10 minutes, so a rider waiting with the screen off is skipped after about 10 minutes, even though they show as online.
evidence: apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts HEARTBEAT_MS comment and startLocationUpdatesAsync({ distanceInterval: 25 }); supabase/migrations/0007_auto_assign.sql 'rl.updated_at > now() - interval 10 minutes'
verifier_note: apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts: the HEARTBEAT_MS setInterval comment says 'while the app is open'. React Native timers pause when the activity is in the background. The background task uses distanceInterval: 25. auto_assign_rider in 0007 requires rl.updated_at > now() - 10 minutes, and smoke.sql confirms that stale riders are skipped. That rider still shows as online. Extra detail: notify-order only alerts the assigned rider, so a skipped rider gets nothing while the order sits in the pool. Staff assigning by hand in admin skips the freshness check, which is a workaround.

title: Location, GPS, battery and notification problems are not handled
detail: If background permission is denied, the app quietly runs foreground-only and does not warn the rider. GPS being switched off is never checked (no hasServicesEnabledAsync). Riders are not asked to exempt the app from battery optimisation, which is a big problem on Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo and Realme phones that kill foreground services. Denied notification permission is not shown. The result: a rider can appear online but be invisible to customers and to assignment.
evidence: apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts startPublishing (if perms.background ... else nothing); apps/rider/src/stores/rider.ts only maps LOCATION_PERMISSION; apps/rider/src/lib/push.ts returns silently when not granted; no battery/hasServicesEnabled code in apps/rider
verifier_note: location.ts startPublishing quietly skips the background task when perms.background is false. There is no hasServicesEnabledAsync, no battery-optimisation prompt, and no check of the 'mocked' flag anywhere in apps/rider. stores/rider.ts turns only LOCATION_PERMISSION into an error message. push.ts returns silently when notification permission is not granted, and Device.isDevice is false on emulators.

title: New-order alerts are weak and there is no accept timer
detail: Automatic assignment never asks the rider to accept, and there is no timeout, so if the rider misses it the order just waits. notify-order sends pushes without a channelId, so Android never uses the high-importance 'orders' channel that push.ts creates. There is no loud repeating ringtone for new orders, and tapping a notification does not open the order (no notification response listener anywhere in apps/). Orders arriving through realtime while the app is open get no sound or vibration. Customer pushes and rider pushes go to every token of the same user, so one person's customer and rider apps receive each other's alerts.
evidence: supabase/functions/notify-order/index.ts sendTo (no channelId, no role filter on push_tokens); apps/rider/src/lib/push.ts setNotificationChannelAsync('orders'); grep addNotificationResponseReceivedListener in apps -> none; 0007_auto_assign.sql assigns directly
verifier_note: supabase/functions/notify-order/index.ts sendTo() sends Expo messages with no channelId, so the 'orders' channel that push.ts creates is never used. It also selects every push_tokens row for the user with no app or role filter; the payload carries role:'rider', but nothing filters on it. No addNotificationResponseReceivedListener or useLastNotificationResponse exists anywhere in apps/. The realtime handler in (tabs)/index.tsx only invalidates queries, with no sound or vibration. auto_assign_rider (0007) assigns directly with no accept step or timeout. Extra detail: orders waiting in the pool alert no rider at all.

title: Riders can go offline or log out while holding orders
detail: rider_set_online(false) and the Log out button in Account never check for assigned orders. Location sharing stops in the middle of a delivery, so the customer's map freezes, and the orders stay assigned to a rider who has logged out.
evidence: supabase/migrations/0007_auto_assign.sql rider_set_online; apps/rider/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx Log out -> setOnline(false).finally(signOut); apps/rider/src/stores/rider.ts setOnline
verifier_note: rider_set_online in 0007 does not check assigned orders, and neither does the online Switch in (tabs)/index.tsx. In account.tsx, Log out runs setOnline(false).finally(signOut) after a 'You will go offline' alert. Extra detail: stores/auth.ts signOut() never deletes the device's push_tokens row. A logged-out phone keeps getting that rider's alerts, and if another rider logs in on it, both riders' alerts go to that phone.

title: No rider support, SOS or safety features
detail: The rider app has no support contact, no SOS or emergency button, no accident insurance information and no help for order problems. It does not use the COMPANY details at all, and COMPANY.supportPhone is still null.
needs_from_owner: Rider support number or WhatsApp, emergency process, accident insurance cover
evidence: grep COMPANY|support|sos|emergency in apps/rider/src -> none; packages/shared/src/company.ts supportPhone: null
verifier_note: A grep for COMPANY, support, sos or emergency in apps/rider/src finds nothing. packages/shared/src/company.ts has supportPhone: null. At minimum, add a 'Call store or support' button on the order screen and the Account tab before launch, since a rider has no way to report gap 8 problems. Insurance information and SOS can come later.

title: No crash reporting, over-the-air updates or forced upgrades
detail: apps/rider has no Sentry or Crashlytics and no expo-updates. Every fix needs a new store build, crashes on riders' phones are invisible, and there is no minimum-version check to force riders onto a fixed build.
needs_from_owner: Crash reporting account (e.g. Sentry free tier)
evidence: apps/rider/package.json dependencies (no expo-updates, no sentry); no version check in apps/rider/src
verifier_note: apps/rider/package.json has no expo-updates and no Sentry or Crashlytics. app.json has no updates or runtimeVersion. There is no version check in apps/rider/src. apps/mobile/eas.json defines channels, but expo-updates is not installed there either.

title: Failed or unconfirmed online payments can charge twice and leave orders stuck
detail: lib/payments.ts gives up on the first 'payment.failed' event, even though Razorpay retry is on and the payment window stays open, so a successful retry is ignored. If verify-payment fails after a successful payment, checkout shows an error, issues a new idempotency key and lets the customer place and pay for a second order. Abandoned 'Awaiting payment' orders are never cancelled or expired, so their stock stays reserved, and the order page has no 'Complete payment' button. This blocks switching on online payments.
evidence: apps/web/src/lib/payments.ts:66 (retry enabled) and :70 (gives up on payment.failed); checkout/page.tsx:81 (new key on any error); no pg_cron or expiry job in supabase/migrations; account/orders/[id]/page.tsx has no pending_payment action
verifier_note: Partly mitigated. razorpay-webhook/index.ts:83-95 handles payment.captured and confirms the order, so a successful retry after payments.ts:70 rejects is not lost on the server. The customer can also cancel an 'Awaiting payment' order from the order page (isCancellableStatus in packages/api/src/status.ts:39 includes pending_payment), which releases the stock. Still open: the client gives up on the first payment.failed even though retry is on (payments.ts:66, 70); checkout issues a new key on any error (checkout/page.tsx:81), so a second order is easy; there is no expiry job (no pg_cron in migrations); and the order page has no 'Complete payment' button. The reviewer missed one case: if an order is cancelled (modal dismissed) and the payment is captured later, confirm_payment (0003:232-266) marks the payment captured but leaves the order cancelled and never refunds it. Online payments are off at launch, so this blocks switching them on, not the launch itself.

title: No bot protection on the public OTP login
detail: The website's login form sends an SMS OTP to any number with no CAPTCHA. Once real MSG91 SMS is on, bots can trigger mass sends that you pay for (SMS pumping). Supabase supports Cloudflare Turnstile or hCaptcha through captchaToken, but none is set up, and the default project-wide SMS rate limit also needs tuning for real traffic.
needs_from_owner: Cloudflare Turnstile (free) or hCaptcha site key and secret
evidence: apps/web/src/app/login/page.tsx:37 (signInWithOtp without captchaToken); supabase/config.toml has no [auth.captcha] section; supabase/functions/send-sms/index.ts has no rate limiting
verifier_note: login/page.tsx:37 calls signInWithOtp with no captchaToken. supabase/config.toml has no [auth.captcha] section, and max_frequency=1s there is local only. send-sms/index.ts has no rate limiting and does not reject non-+91 numbers on the server; the 10-digit Indian check is client-side only (lib/phone.ts). The risk is bounded at launch: Supabase's per-number resend interval (60s) and project-wide SMS hourly cap still apply, and MSG91 DLT routes are India-only by default. I downgraded it to important, but add Turnstile together with the WhatsApp OTP work and before raising the SMS cap or doing any marketing.

title: No way to report missing or damaged items on a delivered order
detail: The refund policy and the app FAQ say customers can report missing or damaged items within 24 hours from the order page. The web order page has no such action, and there is no issue table in the database. Admin can only cancel orders that are not yet delivered and cannot give partial refunds or wallet credit, so these complaints can only be handled by hand.
needs_from_owner: Refund rules (time window, whether a photo is needed, wallet or original payment method)
evidence: apps/web/src/app/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx (actions are only Cancel and Reorder); no complaint or order-issue table in supabase/migrations; apps/admin/src/app/orders/[id]/page.tsx:81 (cancel hidden once delivered)
verifier_note: The web order page has only Cancel and Reorder. No issue or complaint table exists in the migrations. The admin cancel button is hidden once an order is delivered (apps/admin/src/app/orders/[id]/page.tsx:81). The only wallet-credit path is an RLS insert policy for admins (0005_staff_rpcs.sql:133), with no UI and no update to profiles.wallet_balance, so even a manual goodwill credit needs SQL. The policy and FAQ promises (refunds/page.tsx:11, apps/mobile/src/app/account/support.tsx:16) depend on this.

title: Address book cannot be edited on the website
detail: The website can only add and pick addresses. There is no edit, delete or set-default option, although addressesApi.update and remove already exist and the mobile app uses them, so a typo in a flat number stays forever.
evidence: apps/web/src/components/location/LocationModal.tsx (only create and select); packages/api/src/addresses.ts (update and remove exist); apps/mobile/src/app/location/form.tsx:70-80 uses them
verifier_note: apps/web/src/components/location/LocationModal.tsx only calls addressesApi.list and create (lines 40, 57). packages/api/src/addresses.ts has update and remove, and apps/mobile/src/app/location/form.tsx:66-80 and :134 use both. This is a small change, since the API already exists.

title: Store opening hours are ignored, and a closed store looks like 'we don't deliver here'
detail: stores.opens_at and closes_at exist but place_order checks only is_open, so orders are accepted at any hour, even though the delivery policy says they are not. When a store is closed, the serving-store lookup returns nothing and the website says 'We are not here yet… does not deliver to this location' instead of 'Closed, opens at 6 AM'.
needs_from_owner: Opening hours for each store
evidence: supabase/migrations/0003_orders_rpc.sql:95 (checks is_open only); 0002_lat_lng_columns.sql:71 ('where s.is_open'); apps/web/src/components/catalog/StoreGate.tsx:16; shipping/page.tsx second paragraph
verifier_note: opens_at and closes_at exist (0001_init.sql:81-82) and the admin can edit them (apps/admin/src/app/stores/page.tsx:29-30), but nothing reads them. place_order checks only is_open (0003_orders_rpc.sql:95). find_serving_store filters 'where s.is_open' (0002_lat_lng_columns.sql:71), so serving_store returns nothing for a closed store, even though it returns opens_at and closes_at. StoreGate.tsx:13-21 then shows 'We are not here yet'. The current workaround is toggling is_open by hand in the admin panel.

title: Website customers get no order updates
detail: notify-order only sends push messages to app devices (Expo, or ntfy on the test stack). Someone who orders on the website hears nothing about cancellations, 'out for delivery' or 'delivered' unless they keep the order page open. There is no web push, SMS, WhatsApp or email update.
needs_from_owner: Choose a channel (WhatsApp templates or SMS through MSG91, or email)
evidence: supabase/functions/notify-order/index.ts (sendTo uses push tokens only); no service worker or web-push code in apps/web/src
verifier_note: sendTo in supabase/functions/notify-order/index.ts:38-55 sends only Expo pushes to push_tokens, or ntfy on the test stack. apps/web/src has no service worker, PushManager or Notification code. Website customers get updates only while the order page is open (realtime channel at account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:43-55). WhatsApp status messages would fit naturally with the planned WhatsApp OTP integration.

title: WhatsApp OTP and verified email are not on the website login (known item)
detail: The login page always sends the code by SMS and has no WhatsApp option or SMS fallback. The account page saves whatever email is typed into profiles.email without verifying it.
needs_from_owner: Meta WhatsApp Business account and an approved authentication template
evidence: apps/web/src/app/login/page.tsx:37 (channel: "sms"); account/page.tsx ProfileForm calls profileApi.update with email
verifier_note: login/page.tsx:37 uses channel 'sms', with no WhatsApp option or fallback; the app and rider logins are the same (apps/mobile/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx:23, otp.tsx:43). The account page ProfileForm saves email straight to profiles with no verification. A more serious problem behind this direct write, which the reviewer missed: the 'profiles self update' policy (0001_init.sql:421) only pins id and role. Since there are no column grants or guard trigger, any logged-in customer can update their own wallet_balance, referred_by or referral_code with the public key and then pay for orders with the RATION wallet. That is a launch-blocker in its own right.

title: Production maps still use free public OpenStreetMap services
detail: Without an Ola Maps key, the website uses public Nominatim, Photon and tile.openstreetmap.org. Their usage policies forbid production traffic (the code comment in mapStyle.ts says 'testing only'), and if they block us, customers cannot set a location or order.
needs_from_owner: Ola Maps account and an API key restricted to the website domain
evidence: apps/web/.env.example (NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPS_PROVIDER=osm); apps/web/src/lib/maps.ts (osm provider); packages/api/src/mapStyle.ts comment
verifier_note: The code side is done. An Ola Maps provider is implemented for geocoding and autocomplete (apps/web/src/lib/maps.ts:110-128) and for tiles (packages/api/src/mapStyle.ts), and it switches on automatically when NEXT_PUBLIC_OLA_MAPS_API_KEY is set (env.ts:9). What remains is configuration: get an Ola key, restrict it to the production domain (it is exposed in the browser), and set it at build time. Without it, the site falls back to nominatim.openstreetmap.org, photon.komoot.io and tile.openstreetmap.org, which mapStyle.ts itself marks 'testing only'. This belongs on the deployment checklist.

title: No error, 404 or loading pages
detail: There is no not-found.tsx, error.tsx or global-error.tsx, so a crash in any page (almost all run in the browser) shows Next's default 'Application error' screen. A wrong product or category link returns a normal page with 'Not available' instead of a real 404.
evidence: Listing apps/web/src/app shows no not-found, error, global-error or loading files; product/[slug]/page.tsx and category/[slug]/page.tsx render an Empty message instead of calling notFound()
verifier_note: apps/web/src has no not-found.tsx, error.tsx, global-error.tsx or loading.tsx, and notFound() is never called. product/[slug]/page.tsx:24 and category/[slug]/page.tsx:78 render an Empty message with HTTP 200. This is low effort; error.tsx matters most because almost every page renders in the browser.

title: No error monitoring or analytics
detail: There is no error tracking (such as Sentry), no page-speed reporting and no analytics, so checkout failures and drop-off after launch cannot be seen.
needs_from_owner: Choose the tools and create the accounts (for example Sentry and Plausible or Umami)
evidence: Searching apps/web/src and package.json for sentry, gtag, analytics, posthog, plausible, umami and web-vitals found nothing
verifier_note: Searching apps/web, mobile, admin, packages, supabase/functions and every package.json for sentry, gtag, posthog, plausible, umami, web-vitals, analytics, bugsnag and clarity found nothing, and there is no instrumentation file. Edge functions only console.error (_shared/http.ts). Adding analytics later triggers the consent work in item 22.

title: Missing security headers, an open image proxy and an open redirect after login
detail: next.config.ts sets no security headers: no CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors (so the checkout page can be framed by another site), Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy for geolocation. images.remotePatterns allows any https host, so /_next/image works as an open image proxy. login/page.tsx sends the user to the ?next= value without checking it, so /login?next=https://evil.example forwards a freshly logged-in user to an outside site.
evidence: apps/web/next.config.ts:8 (hostname '**', no headers()); apps/web/src/app/login/page.tsx:13 and :23 (router.replace(next))
verifier_note: apps/web/next.config.ts:8 allows remotePatterns hostname '**' and has no headers(). login/page.tsx:13 and :23 pass ?next= straight to router.replace, and the App Router does a full-page navigation for an absolute or '//' URL, so the redirect is real. All three are small fixes. The reviewer missed a far bigger security gap: profiles RLS (0001_init.sql:421) lets customers edit their own wallet_balance (see item 14), which needs a column-level REVOKE or a guard trigger before launch. Related: 'products staff write' (0001:435) uses is_staff(), so store staff can change catalogue-wide prices.

title: No picking or packing flow
detail: Packing is a single status button. The card shows a comma-joined list of item names. There is no pick list sorted by shelf, no per-item check-off, no barcode scanning, and no printable packing slip or bag label. Products have no barcode/EAN or shelf/bin location column to build these from.
needs_from_owner: Whether to print (thermal printer model) and the shelf or bin numbering scheme for the dark store.
evidence: apps/admin/src/app/orders/page.tsx OrderCard (order_items.map(...).join(', ')). The products table in supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql, 0009 and 0010 has no barcode or location column. There is no print view in apps/admin/src/app.
verifier_note: Confirmed. OrderCard in apps/admin/src/app/orders/page.tsx joins item names with commas. products in 0001, 0009 and 0010 has no barcode, EAN, SKU or shelf location column. There is no print route in apps/admin/src/app. Priority lowered: with one store and low launch volume, staff can pack from the order detail page. A simple printable pick list or slip is a quick win. Barcode and bin locations can come later.

title: Low-stock threshold hard-coded at 5 with no alerts
detail: The low-stock threshold is fixed at 5 units for every product, in both the UI and the dashboard RPC. There is no per-product reorder level and no notification. Products never stocked at a store (no inventory row) are not counted as low.
evidence: apps/admin/src/app/inventory/page.tsx (available <= 5). supabase/migrations/0005_staff_rpcs.sql:126 (quantity - reserved <= 5, counting inventory rows only). No reorder_level column in inventory (0001_init.sql).
verifier_note: Confirmed with a small correction. The threshold is 5 in inventory/page.tsx and in staff_dashboard (0005_staff_rpcs.sql:126). There is no reorder_level column and no notification. The correction: the Inventory page's 'Low stock only' filter does include products with no inventory row (the !i branch), and those rows show 0 and are highlighted. Only the dashboard count skips them. A fixed threshold is workable for launch.

title: Coupons and banners cannot be scheduled or targeted
detail: Both tables have starts_at and ends_at, but neither form exposes them, so promotions cannot be scheduled. Coupons cannot be deleted or limited to a store or customer group. Every active coupon code can be read by anyone through the public read policy, so private codes are impossible. Banner links do not support a URL target, and the product target is an unchecked slug typed by hand.
evidence: supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql coupons and banners starts_at/ends_at, and the 'coupons public read' policy. apps/admin/src/app/coupons/page.tsx and banners/page.tsx forms. packages/api/src/admin.ts CouponRow has starts_at and ends_at, unused by the forms.
verifier_note: Confirmed. starts_at and ends_at exist on both tables (0001), and the customer queries respect them (packages/api/src/catalog.ts:96 and coupons.ts:19). The forms in apps/admin/src/app/coupons/page.tsx and banners/page.tsx do not expose them. Coupons have no delete. Banners do have delete. 'coupons public read' makes every active code readable by anyone; that is intended for the checkout coupon list, but it rules out private codes. The banner target is category or product slug only (typed by hand), and the 'url' type noted in the schema comment is not offered.

title: Push tokens stay registered after logout
detail: Apps upsert push_tokens on login but never delete them on sign-out, and a token can belong to several users. After an account switch on a shared phone, the old account's order updates, including the address, keep arriving.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts:36 and apps/rider/src/lib/push.ts:36 (upsert only). apps/mobile/src/stores/auth.ts:48 signOut does not touch push_tokens. 0001_init.sql push_tokens PK (user_id, token).
verifier_note: Confirmed. apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts:36 and apps/rider/src/lib/push.ts:36 upsert only. signOut at apps/mobile/src/stores/auth.ts:48 and apps/rider/src/stores/auth.ts:46 never deletes the token, and the PK is (user_id, token). One correction: the pushes do not include the address. notify-order MESSAGES carry only the order number and status, and RLS blocks opening the old order. So the leak is limited to the order number and status. It is still a few lines to fix.

title: Rider payouts, Cashfree and support chat
detail: Known items, confirmed missing in the backend. There are no payout, earnings-rate or settlement tables. Riders see only tips and cash to deposit. payments.provider defaults to 'razorpay' and the cancel, refund and webhook code is Razorpay-only, so Cashfree needs a provider abstraction. There are no support ticket or chat tables.
needs_from_owner: Rider pay model. RazorpayX/Cashfree accounts (need GSTIN/KYC)
evidence: docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md 'Not implemented'. 0006_rider.sql rider_summary. supabase/functions/_shared/razorpay.ts is the only gateway. 0001_init.sql payments.provider default 'razorpay'.
verifier_note: Confirmed. docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md lists both as not implemented. rider_summary (0006) covers only tips and cash. supabase/functions/_shared/razorpay.ts is the only gateway, and payments.provider defaults to 'razorpay' (0001:298), so Cashfree needs a provider abstraction across place-order, verify, webhook and cancel. No ticket or chat tables exist. Also missed: apps/rider/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx:27 promises 'Payouts are settled weekly to your registered bank account', but there are no rider bank, KYC, vehicle or licence fields anywhere.

title: Small RLS tightening
detail: Reviews can be edited after insert to point at another product, because the eligibility trigger runs on insert only and the policy covers all commands. Any user can write a rider_locations row for themselves. Every active coupon, including private codes, and exact stock counts are readable without login.
evidence: 0001_init.sql:476 'reviews owner write' for all + 0004 trigger 'before insert' only. :463 rider_locations self write (no role check). :428 inventory public read, :430 coupons public read.
verifier_note: Confirmed. 'reviews owner write' covers all commands (0001:476), but check_review_eligibility runs before insert only (0004), so an update can move a review to another product. 'rider_locations self write' (:463) has no role check; this is harmless for assignment because auto_assign_rider joins role='rider', but it lets users write junk rows. 'inventory public read' (:428) exposes exact stock, and 'coupons public read' (:430) exposes every active code with its limits and usage counts.

title: Scaling: indexes and realtime load
detail: No index on orders(created_at) for dashboard counts, wallet_transactions(order_id) (scanned by the referral trigger on every delivery), or refunds(payment_id). Rider GPS updates every 5 s fan out through postgres_changes, with an RLS EXISTS check per subscriber. Moving to Realtime Broadcast, and moving assign_waiting_orders out of the order trigger, will matter as volume grows.
evidence: 0001_init.sql index list. 0004 reward_referral_on_delivery filters by order_id. apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts:54 timeInterval 5000. 0007_auto_assign.sql orders_auto_assign_trigger calls assign_waiting_orders synchronously.
verifier_note: Confirmed. There is no index on orders(created_at) (orders_user_idx leads with user_id), wallet_transactions(order_id) (queried by the referral trigger, 0004) or refunds(payment_id). apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts:54 publishes every 5 s or 15 m through postgres_changes on rider_locations. orders_auto_assign_trigger (0007) calls assign_waiting_orders synchronously, up to 50 orders, inside the delivering or cancelling transaction.

title: Loose fruit and vegetables use fixed weights and fixed prices
detail: Produce is listed as exact weights ('1 kg') at a fixed MRP-style price. Real produce varies in weight and its market price changes daily. Nothing handles approximate weights ('approx 4-6 pcs'), small over- or under-weight adjustments, or a quick daily price update for produce.
needs_from_owner: Daily produce pricing source and process
evidence: supabase/catalog/products/vegetables-fruits.json (Potato 1 kg MRP 5000 / price 3900, Lady Finger 500 g, ...). order_items stores a fixed unit_price (0001_init.sql). There is no variable-weight field.

title: Appliances and electronics need warranty, return and safety-mark handling
detail: The catalogue includes about 14 electrical appliances priced up to about ₹5,500 (mixer grinders, induction cooktop, hair dryers, straighteners, trimmers). The E-Commerce Rules require warranty and guarantee information. Many of these need BIS marks, and returns work differently from groceries (dead on arrival, manufacturer warranty). The schema has no warranty or return-window field, and the policies treat all items the same.
needs_from_owner: Decide whether to sell appliances at launch; supplier warranty terms
evidence: supabase/catalog/products/kitchenware-appliances.json (Preethi Mixer Grinder ₹5,000, Prestige Induction Cooktop ₹3,000, Philips Toaster). hair.json (Philips Hair Dryer ₹1,899, Braun Beard Trimmer ₹2,799). No warranty or return fields in 0001_init.sql products.

title: Recycled phone numbers and no way to change your number
detail: The phone number is the only identity, and there is no change-number flow. In India a disconnected number can be given to a new person after about 90 days. That person logs in by OTP and gets the old owner's saved addresses, order history and wallet balance.
evidence: 0001_init.sql profiles.phone unique. Login only uses supabase.auth.signInWithOtp by phone (apps/mobile/src/app/(auth), apps/web/src/app/login). apps/mobile/src/app/account/profile.tsx can edit name and email only.

title: No waitlist for unserviceable locations
detail: When a location is outside every zone, the customer is just told to try another address. Nothing records where demand is coming from or offers 'notify me when you launch here', which is the main signal for choosing the next dark store.
evidence: apps/web/src/components/location/LocationModal.tsx line 171 'Not serviceable yet. Try another location.' apps/mobile/src/app/location/confirm.tsx lines 65-66. apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx line 74. The searched location is never stored.

title: No way to send promotional messages to customers
detail: The admin can only edit banners and coupons. There is no promotional push, SMS or WhatsApp campaign tool, and no record of marketing consent or opt-out, which TRAI and the DPDP Act require before sending such messages.
needs_from_owner: WhatsApp Business or SMS promotional templates and sender approval (DLT)
evidence: apps/admin/src/app has banners and coupons pages only. supabase/functions/notify-order/index.ts sends order-status messages only. No consent or opt-in column in 0001_init.sql profiles. A search for marketing, consent and opt_in in migrations and admin finds nothing.

title: Optional verified email not implemented
detail: Email is saved as typed, with no verification, and nothing ever sends to it. Verification is needed before it can be used for receipts or account recovery (known item, confirmed).
needs_from_owner: Email sending provider and domain setup (DKIM is deferred to the to-do list)
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/account/profile.tsx (regex check, then profiles.update). No email sender in supabase/functions.
verifier_note: Confirmed. profile.tsx regex-checks the email and writes it straight to profiles. No verification flow exists, and no email sender exists in supabase/functions (send-sms is the only messaging function). Known item.

title: Ratings are collected but never shown
detail: rating_avg and rating_count are kept up to date but never displayed on product cards or the product page. RateItem never loads the user's existing rating, so the stars appear empty when the order is reopened. There is no rating for the delivery or rider.
evidence: supabase/migrations/0004_referrals_reviews_search.sql:77. Searching apps/mobile/src and packages/api/src for rating_avg: nothing. apps/mobile/src/app/order/[id].tsx renders <RateItem> without the initial prop.
verifier_note: Confirmed. rating_avg and rating_count are added at 0004:77 and kept updated by the product_reviews_refresh trigger, but nothing in apps or packages/api reads them; they appear only in database.types.ts. Display is easy because 'reviews public read' exists (0001:475). order/[id].tsx renders <RateItem> without initial, and RateItem never fetches the existing rating. There is no rider or delivery rating.

title: Browsing and product page polish
detail: The product page shows only images[0] (no gallery), with no similar products and no share button. There are no sort or filter options (price, brand, veg). Category lists stop at 120 or 200 items with no pagination. Popular searches are a hard-coded list, there is no recent-search history, and there is no 'notify me' for out-of-stock items.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/product/[slug].tsx. apps/mobile/src/app/category/[slug].tsx (catalogApi.products(storeId, ids, selected ? 200 : 120)). apps/mobile/src/app/search.tsx SUGGESTIONS constant. apps/mobile/src/components/catalog/AddButton.tsx (out-of-stock state cannot be tapped).
verifier_note: Confirmed. product/[slug].tsx uses images[0] only and has no similar items or share button. category/[slug].tsx calls catalogApi.products(storeId, ids, selected ? 200 : 120) with no pagination and no sort or filter. Current sample shelves stay well under these limits. search.tsx:16 has a hard-coded SUGGESTIONS list and no recent searches. AddButton.tsx shows a non-tappable 'Out of stock' with no notify-me option.

title: No website links into the app; deep links bypass login
detail: The ration:// scheme exists, but there are no iOS associated domains or Android app links, so website product links never open the app. Cart, product, order, account and location screens sit outside the login guard, so a deep link opened while logged out loads them with no session.
needs_from_owner: Hosting the assetlinks.json and apple-app-site-association files on the website domain
evidence: apps/mobile/app.json (scheme only; no ios.associatedDomains or android.intentFilters). apps/mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx protects only (tabs) and (auth).
verifier_note: Confirmed. app.json has scheme 'ration' only, with no ios.associatedDomains or android.intentFilters, and the website has no apple-app-site-association or assetlinks.json. _layout.tsx guards only (tabs) and (auth), so cart, product, order, account and location are reachable logged out. The impact is small: catalogue data is public, and order placement fails server-side with UNAUTHENTICATED.

title: Accessibility gaps
detail: Many icon-only buttons have no screen-reader label: Account copy/share, cart close, product back and search, order back, location close and address edit. The address-form checkbox and the payment and address cards do not report checked or selected state.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx, cart.tsx Header, product/[slug].tsx, order/[id].tsx, location/index.tsx, location/form.tsx checkbox, components/checkout/OptionCard.tsx (no accessibilityState). Only 11 files use any accessibilityLabel or accessibilityRole.
verifier_note: Confirmed. 11 files under apps/mobile/src use accessibilityLabel or accessibilityRole. Only components/ui/Button.tsx and category/[slug].tsx use accessibilityState. The icon-only Pressables have no labels: account.tsx copy/share, the cart.tsx Header close, product/[slug].tsx back/search, order/[id].tsx back. components/checkout/OptionCard.tsx and the location/form.tsx checkbox do not report selected or checked state.

title: No usage analytics
detail: There is no event tracking for the funnel (app open → location → add to cart → checkout → order), search terms with no results, or retention, so growth decisions would be guesswork.
needs_from_owner: Choice of analytics tool
evidence: Searched apps/mobile for analytics / posthog / amplitude / mixpanel / firebase: none.
verifier_note: Confirmed. No analytics, posthog, amplitude, mixpanel or firebase in apps/mobile or apps/web. Searches that return nothing are not logged server-side either.

title: Wallet and refund visibility limits
detail: The wallet can only be picked when it covers the whole total; it cannot be combined with cash or online payment. Cancelled online orders show only 'Cancelled', with no refund status or reference.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/cart.tsx (wallet option disabled when walletBalance < bill.total). apps/mobile/src/app/order/[id].tsx (no refund details).
verifier_note: Confirmed. In cart.tsx the wallet OptionCard is disabled when walletBalance < bill.total, and place_order takes one payment_method, so splitting needs schema and RPC changes. order/[id].tsx shows no refund status. The data is already readable through the 'refunds read' and 'payments read' policies (0001:456-458), so showing it is UI-only. Wallet refunds already appear in account/wallet.tsx through wallet_transactions.

title: Account settings, language and logout cleanup
detail: There are no notification or marketing preferences and no Hindi or regional languages. Logout leaves the cart and delivery location on the phone for the next user. The login session is stored in plain AsyncStorage even though expo-secure-store is installed but unused.
needs_from_owner: Which languages to support
evidence: apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/account.tsx. Searched for i18n / expo-localization: none. apps/mobile/src/stores/auth.ts signOut. apps/mobile/src/lib/supabase.ts storage: AsyncStorage. Searched src for SecureStore: none.
verifier_note: Confirmed. account.tsx has no notification or marketing preferences. No i18n or expo-localization. signOut in stores/auth.ts does not clear the cart (ration.cart) or location (ration.location), and the location keeps the previous user's addressId and address line. Fold this cleanup into the item 11 push_tokens fix. lib/supabase.ts uses AsyncStorage, and expo-secure-store is installed but unused. Supabase's RN guide uses AsyncStorage, and SecureStore has a size limit, so this means encrypting with a key held in SecureStore rather than a direct swap.

title: No automated tests for the mobile app
detail: CI only type-checks and lints apps/mobile. The Playwright end-to-end tests cover the website only, so checkout, payment and tracking in the app are not regression-tested.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml (only 'npm run lint -w @ration/mobile' for mobile). No *.test.* files under apps/mobile.
verifier_note: Confirmed for the app UI, but the impact is overstated. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs typecheck for all workspaces and lint for mobile, with no *.test.* files under apps/mobile. However, the shared backend the app uses is regression-tested: supabase/tests/smoke.sql covers place_order, cancel and auto-assign; deno check covers every edge function; tests/e2e/storefront.spec.ts drives checkout through the same place-order function and packages/api. Only the app's own screens and native payment and push paths are untested.

title: No email sending service (DKIM deferred by owner)
detail: Profiles collect an email 'for order invoices', but no email provider is integrated, so no receipts or order emails go out. The planned optional verified email also needs custom SMTP in Supabase Auth, because the built-in sender is heavily rate-limited and only reaches team members. SPF, DKIM and DMARC for zrainbowpride.com stay on the to-do list, as the owner asked.
needs_from_owner: Choice of email provider and DNS records on zrainbowpride.com
evidence: Searching for resend|sendgrid|postmark|smtp|nodemailer|mailgun|ses|zeptomail|brevo finds no integration. apps/mobile/src/app/account/profile.tsx:45 and apps/web/src/app/account/page.tsx:28 have the hint 'For order invoices'.
verifier_note: Confirmed. Searching apps, packages, functions and config.toml for resend, sendgrid, postmark, smtp, mailgun, zeptomail, brevo or ses finds only the OTP 'Resend code' timer. The profile email hint 'For order invoices' is at apps/web/src/app/account/page.tsx:28 and apps/mobile/src/app/account/profile.tsx:45. Priority lowered to later: receipts can live in the app and on WhatsApp at launch. Custom SMTP is needed only when the optional verified email is switched on. SPF, DKIM and DMARC stay on the to-do list as the owner asked.

title: Website not search-engine friendly
detail: Every storefront page is a client component and product pages need a location before they render, so search engines see no product content. There is no robots.txt, sitemap, metadataBase, Open Graph tags or per-product metadata. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is defined but never used. There is no PWA manifest and no universal or app links (apple-app-site-association, assetlinks.json) for ration:// deep links.
evidence: apps/web/src/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx is 'use client' and wrapped in StoreGate. No robots, sitemap, manifest or opengraph files under apps/web/src/app. apps/web/public has only maplibre. env.siteUrl in apps/web/src/lib/env.ts has no consumers.
verifier_note: Confirmed. apps/web/src/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx is 'use client' and wrapped in StoreGate. The app directory has no robots, sitemap, manifest or opengraph files. layout.tsx metadata has no metadataBase or openGraph. env.siteUrl (apps/web/src/lib/env.ts:13) has no consumers. apps/web/public holds only maplibre/. There are no .well-known app or universal links.

title: CI and repo hardening
detail: No Dependabot or Renovate, no CODEOWNERS and no documented branch protection (the catalog bots push straight to main, app and web). The mobile apps are never built in CI: expo-doctor exists but is not run. There is no admin end-to-end test, and no scheduled smoke test against the Razorpay test mode or the real MSG91 sandbox.
evidence: The .github folder holds only workflows/. apps/mobile/package.json has a 'doctor' script that ci.yml never calls. tests/e2e/storefront.spec.ts covers only the storefront. .github/workflows/catalog-images.yml runs 'git push origin HEAD:main' and 'HEAD:app HEAD:web'.
verifier_note: Confirmed. .github contains only workflows/: no dependabot.yml and no CODEOWNERS. The 'doctor' script exists only in apps/mobile/package.json (the rider app has none) and ci.yml never runs it or builds the Expo apps. tests/e2e has only storefront.spec.ts and helpers.ts, so no admin or rider tests. catalog-images.yml:59-61 and catalog-auto-photos.yml:54-55 push straight to main, app and web. Small correction: these workflows also run on push to main for catalog paths (catalog-images.yml:14), not only on manual dispatch.

title: No store pickup details, store navigation or store linking
detail: The order screen loads only store_id. The 'Head to the store' card shows no store name or address and has no navigate button, and Navigate goes only to the customer. Riders are not tied to a store. The pool is not filtered by store or distance, and rider_claim_order does not check that the rider is online or nearby. This matters as soon as there is more than one store.
evidence: apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx ORDER_COLUMNS and navigate(); packages/api/src/rider.ts pool() has no store filter; 0006/0007 rider_claim_order checks role and active count only
verifier_note: apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx ORDER_COLUMNS loads only store_id. The 'Head to the store' card has no name or address, and navigate() goes only to the customer, although the stores table is publicly readable. pool() in packages/api/src/rider.ts has no store or distance filter. rider_claim_order (0007) checks only the role and the 3-order cap; 'online' is enforced only by the disabled button in pool.tsx. I lowered it to later: there is a single dark store at launch and the riders know where it is. It becomes important with a second store.

title: Calls show the customer's real phone number
detail: The Call button opens tel: with the customer's real recipient_phone. A masked calling bridge would protect customer privacy and also stop riders contacting customers after the delivery.
needs_from_owner: Account with a number-masking provider (e.g. Exotel, Knowlarity, Plivo)
evidence: apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx Linking.openURL(`tel:${phone}`)
verifier_note: apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx Call opens Linking.openURL(`tel:${phone}`) with address_snapshot.recipient_phone. I lowered it to later: a masked calling service (for example Exotel) costs money. The cheap fix in gap 5 (hide the phone once the order is delivered or cancelled) covers most of the risk at launch.

title: 'Today' totals reset at 05:30 IST instead of midnight
detail: rider_summary and the tie-break in auto_assign_rider use date_trunc('day', now()). No timezone is set in the migrations, and the Supabase database runs in UTC, so 'Delivered today', 'Tips today' and 'Cash to deposit' reset at 05:30 IST. A night shift's cash vanishes from the screen partway through.
evidence: supabase/migrations/0006_rider.sql rider_summary; 0007_auto_assign.sql order-by subquery; grep Asia/Kolkata|timezone in supabase/migrations -> none
verifier_note: rider_summary (0006) and the tie-break in auto_assign_rider (0007) use date_trunc('day', now()), and so does staff_dashboard in 0005, which affects the admin dashboard too. No timezone appears in supabase/migrations or config.toml. The priority is exaggerated, though. Stores default to 06:00-23:59 (0001 lines 81-82), and a UTC day runs from 05:30 to 05:29 IST, so it covers the whole trading day. The numbers are only wrong for a store open past 05:30 IST. It is a one-line fix ((now() at time zone 'Asia/Kolkata')::date) to fold into the gap 3 ledger work.

title: Rider login is SMS only (no WhatsApp OTP)
detail: The rider app hardcodes SMS for sending and verifying the OTP, so the planned WhatsApp-first login with SMS fallback has to be added here as well as in the customer app and website.
needs_from_owner: WhatsApp Business account and approved OTP template (same as the customer app)
evidence: apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/index.tsx channel: 'sms'; apps/rider/src/app/(auth)/otp.tsx verifyOtp type 'sms' and resend channel 'sms'
verifier_note: (auth)/index.tsx uses channel 'sms'. (auth)/otp.tsx uses verifyOtp type 'sms' and resend channel 'sms'. However, every OTP goes through the Supabase Send SMS hook (supabase/functions/send-sms, config.toml [auth.hook.send_sms]), which takes precedence over the provider. WhatsApp-first with SMS fallback can therefore be decided server-side in that hook, and the rider app keeps working as is. The app needs only new text and perhaps a 'send by SMS instead' button. This rides on the known WhatsApp OTP item and is not separate rider work.

title: English only, no regional languages
detail: Every rider-facing string is hardcoded in English. Most delivery partners would be better served in Hindi or the local language.
needs_from_owner: Which languages to support
evidence: No i18n library in apps/rider/package.json; strings inline in apps/rider/src/app/**
verifier_note: No i18n library in apps/rider/package.json. All strings are inline in apps/rider/src/app/** and components.

title: No offline handling for status taps or location
detail: If the network drops when the rider taps Delivered, it just shows an error. Status changes are not queued for retry, and positions taken while offline are thrown away (catch blocks ignore them), so the route has gaps.
evidence: apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx useMutation onError; apps/rider/src/lib/location.ts publishPosition().catch(() => undefined)
verifier_note: In apps/rider/src/app/order/[id].tsx, the advance mutation onError only sets an error. lib/query.ts sets no mutation retry, so TanStack's default of 0 applies. location.ts drops positions in catch blocks (.catch(() => undefined) and the empty catch in the task).

title: No order batching or multi-drop routing
detail: auto_assign_rider only picks riders with no unfinished orders. Riders can claim up to 3 orders from the pool, but nothing groups nearby orders or orders the drops.
evidence: supabase/migrations/0007_auto_assign.sql 'not exists ... rider_busy_statuses()'; rider_claim_order v_active >= 3
verifier_note: auto_assign_rider (0007) skips any rider with an order in rider_busy_statuses(). rider_claim_order allows up to 3 orders through the pool, with no grouping or drop order.

title: No rider ratings, shifts, incentives or detailed history
detail: Customers cannot rate riders. There are no shift slots or break status, no 'arrived at store' or 'arrived at customer' timestamps for timing reports, no incentives, and History stops at 50 orders with no date filter and no earnings per order.
